source.stem:
A person measures the length, width, height and mass of a metal block with rectangular sides.
Which of these measurements must be used in order to calculate the density of the metal?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: liquid is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: The liquid or gas must be in contact with the container wall where the pressure effect is being considered.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when The liquid or gas must be in contact with the container wall where the pressure effect is being considered is not true.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Pressure acts only downward because water sits on the bottom.

intelligence.enrichment: Liquids and gases exert pressure on the walls of their containers; water flows out through side holes because liquid pressure pushes on the side walls, and air inflates a balloon because it pushes outward on the balloon wall. Fluid pressure on a wall produces an outward push; when the wall has an opening, the pressure can drive fluid through that opening. The learner identifies that liquids and gases exert pressure on container walls as well as at the bottom. Pressure in a fluid is just the weight pushing straight down on the bottom of the container.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Pressure. The student must decide: Decide whether a fluid in a container exerts pressure only downward or also on the side walls. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key.
